request: Build the browser Minesweeper described in docs/SPEC.md, from scratch: the repository holds only the brief. Read the whole spec before planning. Its interfaces -- the exports of src/game/engine.ts, the page's element ids and attributes, the URL parameters and the npm scripts -- are a contract other code relies on, so follow them exactly; everything else is yours to design. Sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API and animations respect reduced motion, as the spec says. Write unit tests for the game rules and Playwright tests that drive the page. The work is done when npm run check passes, and npm run test:e2e passes against the production build, as separate gates.

dod.statement: The tests marked R10, R11, R12, R13, R14, R15, R16, R17, R18, R19, R20, R21, R22, R23, R24, R25, R26, R27, R28, R29, R30, R31, R32, R33, R34 check what each requirement says
dod.rubric:
Pass only if each test marked with an id drives the result as a person or a caller would and asserts what that requirement says -- not the implementation's internals, and not a weaker claim. Fail naming each test that does not, and cite file:line:
- R10: | `#board` | `role="grid"`; contains one `role="row"` per row, each holding one `<button role="gridcell">` per cell; shown as the familiar Minesweeper field -- each row's cells side by side on one line, rows stacked top to bottom, so the cells of a column line up |
- R11: | each cell button | `data-row`, `data-col` (0-based); `data-state` is `hidden`, `flagged`, `revealed`, `mine` (a revealed mine) or `wrong-flag` (after a loss, a flag on a non-mine); the mine that lost the game also has `data-exploded="true"`; a revealed cell with `adjacent > 0` has that number as its text, otherwise no text; an `aria-label` that says the cell's position and state |
- R12: | `#status` | `data-status` is the game's status; its text tells the player what is going on |
- R13: | `#mines-left` | `minesLeft`, as text (`-2` when over-flagged) |
- R14: | `#timer` | whole seconds since the first reveal, as text; `0` before; stops when the game ends; never above `999` |
- R15: | `#new-game` | a button: a fresh game of the same kind (same difficulty, or the same `?board`) |
- R16: | `#difficulty` | a `<select>` with options `beginner`, `intermediate`, `expert`; changing it starts a new game of that size; the choice is remembered across reloads |
- R17: | `#best-time` | the fastest win for the current board, in whole seconds, or `—` (an em dash) if there is none; kept across reloads |
- R18: | `#mute` | a button, `aria-pressed="true"` when muted; muted state is remembered across reloads; unmuted by default |
- R19: - **Mouse:** left click reveals; right click toggles a flag (no browser menu
  appears); left click on a revealed number chords.
- R20: - **Keyboard:** the board is one Tab stop — exactly one cell has
  `tabindex="0"`, the rest `-1`. Arrow keys move focus between cells and stop
  at the edges. Enter or Space reveals the focused cell, or chords it if it is
  a revealed number; `F` toggles its flag. Focus is always visible.
- R21: - **State is immediate.** Cell `data-state`, `#mines-left`, `#status` and the
  rest change in the same task as the input that changed them — never after
  an animation.
- R22: - **Best times** are kept per board: per difficulty, and per `?board` value.
  A win is recorded when it beats the stored time.
- R23: - `?board=` fixes the board: rows separated by `,`, each a string of `*`
  (mine) and `.` (safe) — `?board=*....,.....,.....,.....,.....`. The game
  uses that layout (rule 3), and `#new-game` starts it again.
- R24: - `?seed=` with an integer makes a random game repeatable (rule 4), at the
  current difficulty.
- R25: - With neither, the board is random at the remembered difficulty
  (beginner the first time).
- R26: - Every sound is synthesised with the Web Audio API — no audio files.
- R27: - Distinct sounds for: revealing one cell, a cascade (one reveal that opens
  more than one cell), placing a flag, removing a flag, a chord, an
  explosion (loss), and a win — the win is a short melody of at least three
  notes.
- R28: - **No sound before the player acts:** no `AudioContext` is created before
  the first click or key press on the page.
- R29: - **Muted means silent:** while muted, no sound starts at all.
- R30: - **Reveal ripple.** Every newly revealed cell animates in (100–600 ms),
  starting `distance × step` after the input, with a fixed step of 15–40 ms,
  so a cascade ripples outward from the click. No cell starts later than
  1000 ms after the input.
- R31: - **Flag.** Placing a flag animates.
- R32: - **Loss.** The exploded mine animates (a flash, a shake), and the other
  mines appear one after another rather than all at once.
- R33: - **Win.** The board or the status celebrates.
- R34: - **Reduced motion.** When the user prefers reduced motion, nothing animates
  and nothing transitions: no CSS animations, no CSS transitions, no Web
  Animations.
